title: Big Tech’s Trillion-Dollar Bet Is Starting to Crack, Investors Are Looking Elsewhere for Profits
excerpt: Big Tech is pouring hundreds of billions into AI every year, but investors are quietly starting to separate the winners from the companies that may never see...

Rich Duprey

Sat, July 25, 2026 at 11:18 AM EDT 4 min read

Quick Read

  • Four hyperscalers are on pace to spend $730 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026, yet investor confidence in their returns is slipping.

  • The 30-day correlation between major AI spenders and semiconductor stocks collapsed from +0.78 to near zero, the lowest reading in 4.5 years.

  • Hyperscalers carry $1.65 trillion in off-balance-sheet AI obligations, making the next winners those who convert spending into durable cash flow.

  • Don't wait: the analyst who called NVIDIA in 2010 just revealed his top 10 AI stocks. See the full list FREE now.

For much of the past year, investing in artificial intelligence felt refreshingly simple. Buy the companies building AI infrastructure or the chipmakers supplying it, and both sides generally moved higher together. That trade is becoming more complicated. Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) and Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) continue raising their AI spending plans, pushing annual capital expenditures toward levels that would have seemed unimaginable just two years ago. 

Yet as the price tag climbs into the hundreds of billions of dollars annually, investors are beginning to ask a more practical question: Who ultimately pays for all this spending, and when does it begin generating acceptable returns?

AI Spending Keeps Rising While Investor Confidence Slips

The AI investment race isn't slowing down. Over the past several weeks, both Alphabet and Meta increased their 2026 capital expenditure outlooks during earnings discussions, adding to an already record-setting spending cycle. Combined with Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), the four largest hyperscalers are now on pace to invest around $730 billion on AI infrastructure in 2026, with Wall Street already anticipating another increase in 2027.

These investments include data centers, networking equipment, AI accelerators, custom silicon, and the enormous power infrastructure needed to support them.

Don't wait: the analyst who called NVIDIA in 2010 just revealed his top 10 AI stocks. See the full list FREE now.

Granted, those investments continue fueling demand for companies such as Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO), Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM), and other semiconductor suppliers. But investors are becoming less convinced that the companies writing the checks will generate returns quickly enough to justify the spending.

在过去一年的大部分时间里，投资人工智能让人感觉非常简单。 买入构建人工智能基础设施的公司或提供人工智能基础设施的芯片制造商，双方通常都会一起走高。 这种贸易正变得更加复杂。 Alphabet（纳斯达克股票代码：GOOG）和 Meta Platforms（纳斯达克股票代码：META）继续提高其人工智能支出计划，将年度资本支出推向两年前似乎难以想象的水平。

然而，随着价格每年攀升至数千亿美元，投资者开始提出一个更实际的问题：谁最终为所有这些支出买单？何时开始产生可接受的回报？

人工智能支出持续增长，而投资者信心下滑

人工智能投资竞赛并未放缓。 过去几周，Alphabet 和 Meta 在收益讨论中均上调了 2026 年资本支出前景，进一步推动了本已创纪录的支出周期。 加上微软（纳斯达克股票代码：MSFT）和亚马逊（纳斯达克股票代码：AMZN），四大超大规模企业目前正计划在 2026 年向人工智能基础设施投资约 7300 亿美元，华尔街已经预计 2027 年将再次增加投资。

公司2026 年人工智能资本支出展望
字母1,950亿至2,050亿美元
元平台1250亿至1450亿美元
微软1900亿美元
亚马逊2000亿美元

这些投资包括数据中心、网络设备、人工智能加速器、定制芯片以及支持它们所需的庞大电力基础设施。

诚然，这些投资继续刺激了对英伟达（纳斯达克股票代码：NVDA）、博通（纳斯达克股票代码：AVGO）、美光科技（纳斯达克股票代码：MU）、台积电（纽约证券交易所代码：TSM）和其他半导体供应商等公司的需求。 但投资者越来越不相信开出支票的公司能够足够快地产生回报以证明支出是合理的。
